title: New Manager Self-Review
description: The purpose of the New Manager Self-Review (NMSR) is to provide newly appointed managers with a structured approach to familiarizing themselves with their new responsibilities.
details: The purpose of the New Manager Self-Review (NMSR) is to provide newly appointed managers with a structured approach to familiarizing themselves with their new responsibilities. The NMSR serves as a valuable tool in acclimating to the intricacies of the office environment. Through this process, managers will gain insights into the operations, strengths, and areas for improvement within their office. This comprehensive review process is designed to help them gain a deep understanding of the office they are now in charge of. By delving into the various workloads and identifying the individuals responsible for specific work, new managers will be better prepared with the knowledge needed to manage their office effectively. The NMSR application is designed to house the NMSR data and MI data online. This centralized platform ensures that managers have easy access to essential information, enabling them to make informed decisions and oversee operations efficiently.

title: Policy Feedback System (PFS)
description: PFS is a web-based application developed by the Office of Decision Support and Strategic Information (ODSSI) that contains records since 2007 on more than 100 million electronic disability claims from the DDS, OHO, and FO levels
details: The Policy Feedback System (PFS) is a web application developed by the Decision Support and Strategic Information Team (DSSIT) that gathers empirical data from individual disability claims to identify policy issues, recommend training, and prioritize workloads. Reports created in PFS are not official MI which suggests some discretion in its use. Therefore, access is limited to administrative, managerial, quality, and training support staff. For security purposes, access is suspended for any user that has not used the application to create a report for twelve consecutive months.Users of PFS can review data and create custom reports based on claimant characteristics, geography, policy, and other factors.  PFS functionality includes: Over 105 report types including mapping and other graphic functions to display empirical data; Statistical analytics such as average, range, and standard deviation; Drill down capability to individual cases, exporting and reporting features, and direct access to the electronic folders, the Request for Program Consultation site, and OHO’s Case Processing and Management System (CPMS); and Availability to users throughout SSA, including Headquarters, Regional Offices, DDSs, FOs, OHO, and OQR.
